items.title: Finite background groupoid and cocycle-weighted gauging data
items.design_state: Step 1 authored; conditional two-group prerequisite status and current readiness are recorded in the batch notes and Step-1 receipt.
items.statement:
Let $K$ be a finite ordered simplicial complex. A **finite background field groupoid** $\mathcal F(K)$ is a small category of declared fields and invertible gauge equivalences, with finitely many isomorphism classes and finite automorphism groups. Its automorphisms retain the multiplicities declared by the field model. A **cocycle/action weight** is a function $W_K:\operatorname{Ob}\mathcal F(K)\to U(1)$ constant on every gauge arrow. Its normalized gauging sum is

$$
Z_K(W_K)=\sum_{[x]\in\pi_0\mathcal F(K)}\frac{W_K(x)}{|\operatorname{Aut}_{\mathcal F(K)}(x)|}.
$$

For the finite $2$-group specialization, fix finite $(G,A,\rho,\beta)$ and let $\mathcal B(K)$ be the explicit background gauge $2$-groupoid: objects are flat $G$-edge cochains and $A$-face cochains satisfying $\delta_aB=a^*\beta$; $1$-arrows retain raw vertex/edge parameters $(g,\lambda)$, and $2$-arrows are vertex cochains $t$ with $\lambda'-\lambda=\delta_{a^g}t$, for fixed $g$. The raw $1$-composition is the displayed $\tau$-corrected composition; its associator is $\beta(k_i,h_i,g_i)$. Write $\pi_0$ for object equivalence classes, $\pi_1(\mathcal B(K),x)$ for $2$-isomorphism classes of $1$-automorphisms, and $\pi_2(\mathcal B(K),x)$ for $2$-automorphisms of the identity $1$-arrow. For a phase weight $W_K$ constant on all $1$-arrows, define the higher normalized gauging sum

$$
Z^{(2)}_K(W_K)=\sum_{[x]\in\pi_0\mathcal B(K)}W_K(x)\frac{|\pi_2(\mathcal B(K),x)|}{|\pi_1(\mathcal B(K),x)|}.
$$

Distinct raw gauge labels are not identified by equality of their effects on fields. The higher sum retains $\pi_2$; it is not ordinary groupoid integration of the $1$-truncation. In particular a point has higher weight $|A|/|G|$ for unit action, whereas an ordinary field groupoid $BG$ has weight $1/|G|$.

For a subcomplex $L\subseteq K$ and fixed field $s$ on $L$, relative fields and arrows use exact restriction to $s$, identity vertex gauge labels on $L$, zero edge gauge labels on $L$, and zero vertex $2$-gauge labels on $L$. Their higher sum uses the same $\pi_2/\pi_1$ prescription. Ordinary groupoids are included as $2$-groupoids with only identity $2$-arrows, so this prescription reduces to the preceding ordinary sum. A higher cocycle supplies an admissible scalar action only after its evaluated weight is proved invariant; nontrivial boundary line-bundle actions require their own transgression data and are not silently treated as scalar functions.

items.title: Finite cocycle-weighted groupoid gauging and gluing
items.design_state: Step 1 authored; conditional two-group prerequisite status and current readiness are recorded in the batch notes and Step-1 receipt.
items.statement:
Let $K=K_1\cup_\Sigma K_2$ be a finite ordered simplicial complex written as a union of two finite subcomplexes with common subcomplex $\Sigma$. Let $\mathcal F$, $\mathcal F_1$, $\mathcal F_2$, and $\mathcal S$ be finite background field groupoids for $K$, $K_1$, $K_2$, and $\Sigma$, with restriction functors $r_i:\mathcal F_i\to\mathcal S$. The homotopy pullback $\mathcal H=\mathcal F_2\times^h_{\mathcal S}\mathcal F_1$ has objects $(x_2,x_1,\alpha)$ with $\alpha:r_2(x_2)\overset{\cong}{\longrightarrow}r_1(x_1)$ and morphisms $(u_2,u_1)$ satisfying $r_1(u_1)\circ\alpha=\alpha'\circ r_2(u_2)$.

Assume that restriction induces an equivalence $J:\mathcal F\to\mathcal H$. Let $W,W_1,W_2$ be $U(1)$-valued cocycle/action weights on these groupoids, and assume that under $J$ the weight factors as $W(x_2,x_1,\alpha)=W_2(x_2)W_1(x_1)$. For each object $s$ of $\mathcal S$, define the homotopy fiber $(\mathcal F_i)_s$ to have objects $(x_i,\eta_i:r_i(x_i)\overset{\cong}{\longrightarrow}s)$ and morphisms $u_i$ satisfying $\eta'_i\circ r_i(u_i)=\eta_i$, and put

$$ Z_i(s):=\sum_{[(x_i,\eta_i)]\in\pi_0((\mathcal F_i)_s)} \frac{W_i(x_i)}{|\operatorname{Aut}_{(\mathcal F_i)_s}(x_i,\eta_i)|}. $$

Then the normalized gauging sums are finite, are invariant under replacement of a field by a gauge-isomorphic field, and satisfy

$$ Z_K(W)= \sum_{[s]\in\pi_0(\mathcal S)} \frac{Z_2(s)Z_1(s)}{|\operatorname{Aut}_{\mathcal S}(s)|}. $$

This is a finite groupoid theorem. A finite cocycle action is covered only when its evaluated weights obey the stated arrow-invariance and gluing-factorization hypotheses.

items.statement:
Fix a finite group $G$, finite abelian group $A$, action $\rho$, normalized $3$-cocycle $\beta$, and a finite ordered simplicial complex $K$. Let $\mathcal B(K)$ be the full background gauge $2$-groupoid, retaining its vertex $2$-gauge transformations, and let $W_K:\operatorname{Ob}\mathcal B(K)\to U(1)$ be constant on $1$-arrows. Let $V_K,E_K$ be the numbers of vertices and edges and define

$$
c(K)=\frac{|A|^{V_K-E_K}}{|G|^{V_K}}.
$$

Then its higher gauging sum satisfies

$$
Z_K^{(2)}(W_K)=\sum_{[x]}W_K(x)\frac{|\pi_2(\mathcal B(K),x)|}{|\pi_1(\mathcal B(K),x)|}=c(K)\sum_{x\in\operatorname{Ob}\mathcal B(K)}W_K(x).
$$

For any subcomplex $L$ and fixed field $s$ on $L$, the higher sum over the relative $2$-groupoid is

$$
Z_{K,L}^{(2)}(s)=\frac{c(K)}{c(L)}\sum_{x|_L=s}W_K(x).
$$

In particular let $K=K_1\cup_\Sigma K_2$, where the intersection is the subcomplex $\Sigma$ and all orders are induced. Assume invariant weights $W_i$ and $W_K$ obey $W_K(x)=W_2(x|_{K_2})W_1(x|_{K_1})$. Put $Z_i(s)=Z_{K_i,\Sigma}^{(2)}(s)$. These boundary functions are invariant on $1$-arrows of $\mathcal B(\Sigma)$ and obey the actual finite $2$-group gluing law

$$
Z_K^{(2)}(W_K)=\sum_{[s]\in\pi_0\mathcal B(\Sigma)}Z_2(s)Z_1(s)\frac{|\pi_2(\mathcal B(\Sigma),s)|}{|\pi_1(\mathcal B(\Sigma),s)|}.
$$

The empty complex has $c=1$ and one empty field. For a point and unit weight the sum is $|A|/|G|$. When $A$ is trivial these formulas reduce to ordinary finite flat $G$-connection normalization. The theorem assumes scalar invariant weights and their stated factorization; it does not assert that an arbitrary higher cocycle defines such boundary scalar data.

title: Finite Groupoid Gauging and Gluing — Examples

items.title: The normalized sum on a one-object finite groupoid
items.design_state: Step 1 authored; conditional two-group prerequisite status and current readiness are recorded in the batch notes and Step-1 receipt.
items.statement: Let $G=C_2=\{1,s\}$ with $s^2=1$. Let $BG$ be the category with one object $*$, with morphisms $\operatorname{Hom}(*,*)=G$ and composition given by multiplication in $G$. Give its unique object the weight $W(*)=1$. The normalized gauging sum of this finite background groupoid is $1/2$.

items.title: A nontrivial cocycle weight on the finite two-element gauge groupoid
items.design_state: Step 1 authored; conditional two-group prerequisite status and current readiness are recorded in the batch notes and Step-1 receipt.
items.statement: Let $G=C_2=\{1,s\}$ and let the finite background groupoid be the conjugation action groupoid $G//G$: its objects are $g\in G$, and an arrow labeled $h\in G$ sends $g$ to $hgh^{-1}$. Define the normalized group 1-cocycle $\chi:G\to U(1)$ by $\chi(1)=1$ and $\chi(s)=-1$, and set $W(g)=\chi(g)$. The action weight is invariant under every arrow, and the normalized gauging sum is zero.

items.title: The homotopy-pullback gluing factor for the two-element group
items.design_state: Step 1 authored; conditional two-group prerequisite status and current readiness are recorded in the batch notes and Step-1 receipt.
items.statement: Let $G=C_2=\{1,s\}$ and let both restriction functors be the identity functor on the one-object groupoid $BG$. Give both pieces and the glued groupoid the constant weight $1$, and define the glued groupoid to be the homotopy pullback $BG\times^h_{BG}BG$. Its normalized gauging sum is $1/2$. Each homotopy fiber of an identity restriction over the unique boundary object has normalized integral $1$, so the gluing formula gives the same value.

items.title: A point retains the second gauge stabilizer
items.statement: Let $K$ consist of one vertex. Take $G=\mathbb Z_2$, $A=\mathbb Z_3$, trivial action and $\beta=0$, with unit phase weight. There is one background object, two distinct raw $1$-automorphisms and three $2$-automorphisms of each. The higher gauging sum is $3/2$. Identifying arrows by their effects on the singleton object set would give $1$; retaining $G$ but discarding $2$-arrows would give $1/2$.

items.title: Split two-group interval gluing with a nontrivial action
items.statement: Let $G=\mathbb Z_2$, $A=\mathbb Z_3$, $\rho_1(t)=-t$, and $\beta=0$. Let $K$ be the ordered interval with vertices $0<1<2$ and edges $01,12$, decomposed into those two edges with intersection the vertex $1$. Give every field unit weight. Each edge and the full interval have higher gauging sum $3/2$. Each relative edge amplitude at the unique boundary field is $1$. The gluing contraction has boundary mass $3/2$ and gives $3/2$ again; discarding that second gauge stabilizer would change the contraction.

items.title: Nonzero Postnikov data retain higher gauge volume on a tetrahedron
items.statement: On the ordered tetrahedron $0<1<2<3$, take $G=A=\mathbb Z_2$ with trivial action and $\beta(g,h,k)=ghk$. This is a normalized $3$-cocycle of nonzero class. There are $64$ background objects, all gauge equivalent. For unit weight the higher sum is $1$, with $\pi_1\cong\mathbb Z_2$ and $\pi_2\cong\mathbb Z_2$ at any background. The nonzero Postnikov cocycle is retained in the gauge transformations and their associator.
